newsitem.title: CANADA: Corriente signs on Arequipa star.
newsitem.headline: Corriente signs on Arequipa star.

text.p: Catherine McLeod-Seltzer, known for engineering the C$1 billion takeover of Arequipa Resources Ltd, has joined the board of Corriente Resources Inc.
McLeod-Seltzer will help with the development of Corriente's Chama bulk-tonnage gold project in central Peru, Corriente said.
McLeod-Seltzer said she looked over the Corriente data on Chama and decided to take on the board position because it reminded her of the Pierina gold deposit in Peru.
"It's early days, but that's what attracted me," she said from Vancouver. "This thing looks like Pierina."

McLeod-Seltzer, who has just got married and changed her name from simply McLeod, was president and chief executive officer of Arequipa until Barrick Gold Corp bought the company last summer for about C$1.0 billion.
Arequipa's main asset was the Pierina gold deposit in Peru.
While many Corriente investors have focused on Corriente's copper prospect in Argentina, McLeod-Seltzer, 36, said she will concentrate on the Peruvian gold.
"I happen to like gold," she said. "I like to be very involved in what's going on."
Corriente also said it has granted stock options for 120,000 shares at a price of C$8.24 per share which can be exercised for three years.
And Corriente said its chief financial officer, William Meek, has resigned from the board but will continue with his CFO responsibilities.
